draft.title: The Persian Wars
card: Persia was a huge empire to the east of Greece. In the early 400s BCE its kings sent armies and ships to invade the Greek city-states.
In 490 BCE the Athenians beat a Persian army at Marathon. In 480 BCE a Persian fleet was defeated at the sea battle of Salamis.
Many city-states, including Athens and Sparta, joined forces to fight Persia. They were usually separate, so this was an unusual step.
After the wars, Athens grew rich and powerful. This led to its golden age, a time of great achievement in art, building and ideas.
draft.remember: Greek city-states united to beat Persia, and Athens' golden age followed.

a.q: Why was the Greek fight against Persia unusual for the city-states?
opts: Many city-states joined forces instead of acting alone
Every city-state fought on the Athenian side only
The city-states had no ships to take part
The city-states joined Persia to fight Athens
a.why: The city-states were usually separate, but many joined forces to face Persia. It is wrong to say only Athens fought, because Sparta and others also took part.
a.clue: Think about how the city-states usually acted.

b.q: Which result followed the Greek victories over Persia?
opts: Athens grew powerful and entered a golden age
Persia took control of Athens and its fleet
Sparta ended its training of boy soldiers
The city-states became one single country
b.why: After the wars, Athens became rich and powerful, which led to its golden age. The city-states did not become one country. They stayed separate, even though they had joined forces for the wars.
b.clue: Think about what happened to Athens after it won.

a.best: Many city-states joined forces instead of acting alone

b.best: Athens grew powerful and entered a golden age
